patches.value: For every t>0, e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable. Moreover, there exist a compact interval J⊂(0,∞) with t∈interior(J) and a compact C⊂ℝⁿ such that u(x,s)=q for x∉C and s∈J; throughout J the fields u_t(·,s), u_{x_j}(·,s), e(·,s), and e_t(·,s) are continuous and vanish outside C.

value.type: compact interval in (0,∞) containing t in its interior

value.declaration: Choose compact C from H003 for J.

patches.value: Fix arbitrary t>0, set J=[t/2,3t/2], and use H003 to choose compact C such that u(x,s)=q for every x∉C and s∈J. The complement of C is open, and u is constant q on its spatial neighborhood for all s∈J. Smoothness therefore implies every first derivative in x and t, as well as the mixed derivatives entering e_t, vanishes off C. The fields u_t,u_{x_j},e,e_t are continuous by smoothness and supported in C. In particular e(·,t) is continuous with compact support. Euclidean opens are measurable, Lebesgue measure is finite on compact sets, and ℝ is a normed additive commutative group; M001 gives integrability of e(·,t). This proves the claimed support and integrability facts for arbitrary t.
